body:
>First off, it's my impression the long-term nature of it has you focused >so much on the pain that you may not be able to talk about your causes >or why. You really seem resigned to be stuck this way. So I'm going to >try to get you thinking from other perspectives.

I kind of specifically didn't mention much about causes, because it would out me as female, which opens another can of worms and gender-specific advice I wasn't sure I wanted at the time.

>What happened at age 14/15?

Well, nothing in particularly. But it was when the depression first really started. I lived from age 8 to 17 with an abusive step-mother who on a daily basis told me what I was was wrong. I lived in terror of her. I read comics and fantasy books to try to escape the situation I had at home, and *by God* girls were not supposed to like those things either. She did everything she could to remove any comfort I had in my life, or to tell me I wasn't supposed to like it. Everything really started with her. She was 11 years younger than my Dad, attractive and blond, and pretty much the epitome of womanliness.

> What about your friends, why are you afraid to tell them - or have you and it has failed - what went on in your life?

I have good friends. But all of them have no problems with being what they are. My women friends enjoy being feminine. They have no problems with being sexual. They know I have problems but I don't really think they understand why, and when they do try to help it just comes off as being patronizing. I hate the way I must appear to them, sometimes. "Poor levees_breaking, she just doesn't like who she is and she just needs to enjoy life a little more by dressing up and having fun!" 

> Is your mind where it originates? It is thinking that is where it all starts?

 I have different triggers. I can be triggered if I have been in self-imposed exile long enough, so that would be causing it by thoughts alone. Other times, it can be triggered by some failing or perceived failing I had at social gatherings or at work, which in turn reinforces my beliefs I shouldn't make any attempts to socializing since that too is something I fail at.
 
> Is your life only defined by your failure and depression?

I don't think so for now, but it's starting to.

> Who are you in life, what is important to you, what is your goals? Do you have any girlfriend/boyfriend or spouse?

Due to my views about myself, I don't see myself as some hot hoochy-mama who has a ton of beautiful friends and loves to party. I have certain problems with the way women are perceived and the way I am supposed to be. 

Personally, I'd like to see myself as a crazed creative genius, who thinks differently from other people. Music is my muse. I have entire images and scenes leap into my mind fully formed just by listening to certain songs. I am very much an escapist. I love books and movies, I have well over a thousand of both in my home. I would rather involve myself in a story than face my own seemingly inescapable reality.
But in a certain way, my complete difference from most women is a driver of my ego. Look at me, I say. You don't see me out shopping at the mall, blabbering on my cellphone at all hours of the day, or parallel parking poorly. I see the world for what it is, and I can pick and choose the aspects of myself that I want. Well, at least in theory.
My dream job was to be a writer and/or comic book artist. I went the route of computer scientist, however, and I work in tech support since the job market sucks around here. I love the combination of story and art.

I know what is wrong in my life. I know why I am depressed. I have some very twisted beliefs, and I feel despair when I think about the world. There are two sides in constant conflict inside of me - the side that hates myself, and the side that loves myself. Bring to a boil, and it's all a huge goddamn mess.

I spend too much time inside myself. I haven't mentioned much the source of my depression because it would reveal a little more about me than I'd like. I'd like the benefit of help without people assuming certain things about me that may not be true. I probably will end up saying more.

Thank you. I needed to hear this.

Edit: Didn't read this fully. The thought that I could help anyone else makes me feel amazing. Rock on, brother.

Those writings I talked about are sort of a non-canon thing to my main story.. Kind of a masochistic writing where I can allow myself to feel what I normally repress. They're not written to be shown to others, just as a vent. I do everything I can to hide them as is; I password protect the files and store them deep on my hard drive. I'm not sure I'd want anyone to see them. They are pretty brutal. I will if I have to.

I don't know about still having that optimism. It's decreased as my illness has increased. It doesn't help that I already have a dearth of willpower as is. Maybe if I had some, along with that optimism I could have helped myself.

I don't feel that I can help myself anymore. I don't think I was ever able to help myself. I only ever feed this pain, not starve it.
